title: Playing it
description: For performers: keys, touch and MIDI, the named controls as expression, Wander as a co-player, offers mid-phrase, and the dock.

lines.text: This is Auracle as an instrument, with chords, lines and swells under your hands.
Two rows of the computer keyboard play notes, with Z and X for octaves.
Hold Shift for an accent.
On the screen keys, strike lower down for a harder note.
A MIDI keyboard brings velocity, pitch bend and the sustain pedal.
In PERFORM, the touch row lets velocity play timbre as well as level.
With Bright on touch, soft notes play darker and hard notes brighter.
The six named controls are your expression, and they mean the same thing on every patch.
Turning them never interrupts a note.
Hold a pad chord and ride Bright up slowly for a swell.
A long press on a control plays what it does on this patch.
The XY pad puts two of them under one finger, Bright across and Motion up.
Wander plays along with you.
A little, and ideas appear in B. More, and the knobs drift toward your taste.
All the way up, it roams.
Touch anything and it waits. Freeze holds it still.
In the middle of a phrase, press Offer.
A variant grows into B and joins the chord you are holding.
Hold Peek to hear it, or ride Blend across at matched loudness.
Take it, or ask for another. Once heard, either answer teaches it.
Keep marks the sound as home.
Back glides you there, so you can wander out for a solo and come back.
In the dock, Hold latches chords, and Unison stacks all four voices on one note.
Glide slides a melody line from note to note, and chords stay clean.
The arpeggiator plays the held chord up, down or both ways, in time with the tempo.
Sync puts the patch's step sequencers on that tempo too.
A controller's first eight knobs claim the eight controls, and Learn remaps any of them.
Pressure pushes Bright, the mod wheel pushes Motion, and MIDI clock sets the tempo.
Booth mode plays by itself when no one is at the keys.
The first touch hands the instrument back.
Nothing in PERFORM opens a dialog, because a player in the middle of a phrase cannot answer one.
